newsitem.title: USA: Dollar falls vs yen on strong Japanese economic report.
newsitem.headline: Dollar falls vs yen on strong Japanese economic report.

text.p: The dollar ended lower against the Japanese yen Wednesday after a report showed surging optimism among big Japanese manufacturers, suggesting Japan's huge trade surplus with the United States will continue to grow, analysts said.
But the dollar rose against the British pound, extending its gains after brokerage firm Goldman Sachs on Tuesday said the pound was 15 percent overvalued.
The dollar fell sharply in Tokyo trading after the Bank of Japan's quarterly report, called the tankan, showed surprising confidence among major Japanese industrialists.

"The tankan was much stronger than anticipated," said John McCarthy, senior vice president at ING Barings. "There's no question we'll see upward pressure on Japanese trade surpluses and slow, but sure upward pressure on the yen."

The yen was also aided by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, who told a European Union summit in the Hague, Netherlands he hoped Europe's proposed single currency would not reduce international usage of the yen.
But after falling more than a yen, the dollar rebounded somewhat by the start of U.S. trading as market players began to focus on a separate tankan index showing weakness among non-manufacturers.
Underlying Japanese economic weakness might prevent the Bank of Japan from raising interest rates, which enhances the appeal of more lucrative dollar-linked investments.

"The implication is that the Bank of Japan is on hold, so the downside for the dollar is limited based on the interest rate differential, which is the main focus of dollar-yen trading," said Mike Malpede, senior foreign exchange analyst at Refco Group, Ltd.

The dollar fell to 113.83 yen late Wednesday from 114.92 on Tuesday. The greenback also fell to 1.7241 German marks from 1.7245. The pound fell to $1.6633 from $1.6695 and the dollar dipped to 1.4379 Swiss francs from 1.4385. The U.S. currency rose to Canadian $1.3942 from C$1.3907.

A report showing weak U.S. durable goods orders in May contradicted strong May existing home sales data and supported the consensus view that Federal Reserve officials will leave interest rates steady when they meet next week, analysts said.
"The U.S. numbers were really offsetting," Malpede said.
The pound fell broadly in Europe amid residual selling after a weekly Goldman Sachs European report called it overvalued on Tuesday.
"That put a lot of pressure on sterling, which fell against the dollar and the deutschemark," Malpede added.
In other European trade, the mark fell to its lowest point in five months against the Italian lira.
Widespread rumours that Italian officials would lower interest rates and talk that the lira would be included in the first round of Europe's monetary union boosted the Italian unit, traders said.
"The prospects for Italy to join on the first round are as good as at any time before, so we're seeing continual interest to buy Italian fixed-income instruments," McCarthy said.
